methodological_rigor.justification: The authors construct a large cross-disease PBMC scRNA-seq atlas (>6.5M cells, 1,047 patients, 19 diseases) integrating in-house cohorts (SCGT00-06) and multiple published datasets. Rigorous preprocessing is described: genotype-based and CellPlex demultiplexing with vireo/Cellsnp-lite, QC thresholds (library size, mitochondrial %, doublet scrubbing), scVI-based batch integration, recursive top-down annotation to 64 subtypes, and adjusted Rand index comparison with original author labels. Pseudobulk edgeR quasi-likelihood F-tests are used for DEGs with BH FDR correction, and explicit train/validation splits into Main, unseen patients, and unseen studies support the classifier evaluation. Remaining gaps: observational cohort assembly introduces confounding across studies, and disease labels are inherited from source cohorts rather than harmonized clinical adjudication.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a cross-sectional atlas/classifier resource spanning 19 diseases including cancers (BRCA, HNSCC, NPC, CRC) alongside autoimmune, infectious and chronic inflammatory conditions, best mapped to Oxford 4 (low-quality/observational cross-sectional series with heterogeneous cohort assembly). Translational relevance is plausible via 'cells as living biomarkers' framing and a patient classifier validated on unseen studies, but no clinical decision threshold, outcome association, or prospective validation is provided. Oncology-specific utility is limited to showing how solid-tumor PBMC signatures cluster relative to other inflammatory conditions.

reporting_quality.justification: No single clinical reporting standard perfectly fits a cross-disease single-cell atlas; reporting largely follows single-cell best practices. Methods comprehensively document sample handling, library chemistry, demultiplexing, QC thresholds, integration (scVI parameters in Supplementary Table 7), annotation markers (Supplementary Table 3), DEG model formula, and reproducibility via a GitHub code repository. Data sources and accession IDs are tabulated; some IDs appear redacted in the normalized text. Ethics approvals per cohort are listed. Minor gaps: patient-level clinical metadata depth varies by cohort and missing age/sex samples are handled by exclusion rather than imputation.

novelty_literature.justification: The scale (6.5M cells, 19 diseases including multiple cancers and autoimmune/infectious conditions) and the attempt to build an explainable inflammation classifier that generalizes to unseen studies are genuinely novel contributions beyond disease-specific PBMC atlases. The integration of curated Cytopus immune gene sets with HVGs and disease-vs-healthy DEGs for an interpretable landscape is a meaningful methodological combination. The work extends rather than redefines the single-cell atlas paradigm (Sikkema, Massoni-Badosa approaches cited).

writing_presentation.justification: Methods are exhaustively detailed with clear subsection structure covering ethics, sample processing, sequencing chemistry, QC, annotation, feature selection, integration and classifier evaluation. Terminology is consistent (CORE vs unseen studies vs unseen patients; Level 1 vs Level 2 annotation). The abstract conveys scope effectively. Density is high and some paragraphs string together many tool names and parameters that could be offloaded to supplementary tables for readability.

key_strengths: Unprecedented scale: 6.5M PBMC single cells from 1,047 patients across 19 diseases including BRCA, HNSCC, NPC and CRC alongside autoimmune, infectious and chronic inflammatory conditions
Rigorous integration pipeline (scVI, vireo genotype demultiplexing, CellPlex hashing) with explicit QC thresholds and adjusted Rand index validation against original annotations
Thoughtful data-split design with both unseen-patient and unseen-study validation sets for the inflammation classifier
Interpretable feature set combining HVGs, healthy-vs-disease DEGs (edgeR quasi-likelihood with BH FDR), and curated Cytopus/inflammation gene sets
Reproducibility supported by GitHub repository and detailed supplementary tables of parameters and annotation markers
key_concerns: Oncology-specific translational implications are limited; no prospective outcome association or decision-threshold demonstration
Disease labels inherited from heterogeneous source cohorts without unified clinical adjudication
Multiple datasets overlap in patients with severity-based sample selection introducing selection bias
Batch effects across studies, chemistry (3'/5', v2/v3) and institutes partially mitigated by scVI but not formally quantified post-integration in the excerpt
No single established reporting standard applied; clinical metadata depth (age/sex/ethnicity) uneven
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically rigorous, large-scale multi-disease PBMC atlas with a credible interpretable classifier; appropriate for a top-tier general-science/medicine venue (Tier 1) with minor revisions around batch-effect quantification and tighter oncology-specific translational positioning.
